params.EMBEDDING_QUERY_PREFIX: Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages:

per_question.query: Why do AI chatbots sometimes make things up, and what are two ways to reduce it?
Is it always better to give an AI more retrieved documents when it answers a question?
Do large language models know when to hold back instead of answering a medical question?
What is the difference between checking an answer by matching words and checking it by meaning?
In RAG, how does the chunk size affect answer quality, and can chunks at several levels (multi-sentence, paragraph, section, document) do better than one level?
How can a token-level hallucination detector for RAG use the retrieved documents to find ungrounded tokens?
Name two approaches that detect hallucination from a language model's internal states instead of its output text.
Is there a single score that combines calibration, robustness and uncertainty to measure how reliable an LLM is?
What is In-Context RALM, and why is it easier to deploy than other retrieval-augmented language models?
How much better is LongRAG than ordinary RAG and long-context LLMs on multi-hop question answering over long documents?
Does the way a prompt is laid out, for example as plain text, Markdown or JSON, change how well a GPT model does the task?
How much does ShotKV improve accuracy on long-context generation tasks, and how much latency does it save compared with running with the full cache?
Can preference tuning on English data alone make a multilingual language model less toxic in other languages?
Does the order of the answer choices change how well an AI model does on a multiple-choice test?
Why can an AI judge give misleading quality scores, and how can a small number of human labels be used to correct them?
How does SetFit differ from LoRA fine-tuning of a large language model when you want to train a text classifier with limited data and hardware?
How does high-precision scoring fix the problem of tied relevance scores when a retrieval system runs in low precision?
Can you tell it not to?
What goes wrong with those methods?
How can a system route questions to different language models while respecting each user's own balance between cost and quality?
How many parameters does GPT-4 have, according to papers that report a figure?
Does that work equally well for every kind of task?
Can the model be protected against that without retraining it?
Is there one best setting for every task?
What have researchers done about gender bias in Chinese text and in machine translation?
How can you tell whether a text was part of a language model's training data: by testing the model, or by searching the training corpus?
How many parameters does the OLMoE language model use for each token, and how much data was it trained on?
How can a language model be made cheaper to run in one specialised domain by changing its vocabulary?
Do language models get better at knowing when they are wrong as they are trained or as they get larger?
How can a question that depends on earlier turns of a conversation be rewritten to stand on its own, and can this be learned without human-labelled data?

A method that keeps attention entropy stable by changing the rotary position embedding base and scaling the attention logits can stretch LLaMA-2-7B-Chat to a 16K-token context; how much fine-tuning does it need?
How accurate is BERT-Large when it is pretrained with differentially private SGD in very large batches, compared with ordinary BERT?
Where do the claims in the MultiFC fact-checking dataset come from, and how well does the best model predict whether a claim is true?
How much of BERT's accuracy does contrastive pruning keep on QQP and MNLI when 97% of the parameters are removed?
For searching legal documents in French, does combining several retrieval models work better than using the best single one?
How can randomly switching off attention heads while training make a speech recognition Transformer better, even though every head is used at test time?
When a language model is asked again and again to improve its own answer without being told what is wrong, what happens over the rounds?
How can a game-theoretic rationalization framework stop a toxic-language detector from linking dialect or identity words to toxicity?
How do SeqXGPT and STADEE differ in the way they detect machine-generated text?
How does grouped-query attention speed up a language model differently from letting only the top-k tokens through each layer, as in mixture-of-depths?
Name one way to find out what a language model knows from its internal activations without labels, and one way to judge how reliable its answers are when you only see its outputs.
In a retrieval-augmented system, is exact nearest-neighbour search worth its cost compared with approximate search, and how can an approximate tree index lose less retrieval quality?
What happens if the questions use brand names instead?
Can they be fooled easily?
How good can it get in a day on one graphics card?
In one study that gave GPT-4 news headlines published after its knowledge cutoff, how well did the model predict the stock market's first reaction?
The first broad evaluation of ChatGPT as a zero-shot Text-to-SQL system used how many benchmark datasets, and in which setting did it beat a fine-tuned state-of-the-art model?
In one study of multilingual instruction tuning, how many multilingual examples added to an English-only tuning set were enough to clearly improve instruction following in other languages?
According to the gradient entanglement analysis of margin-based alignment losses, why can training make a language model more likely to produce the response it was told to avoid?
In one comparison across nine language models, how did putting distractor options into the prompt change how well the models' stated confidence matched their correctness?
How can soft prompts help a LLaMA-7B model that has been compressed with 4-bit quantization and 50% weight pruning to recover its accuracy?

How does fine-tuning a translation model with nearest-neighbour statistics differ from kNN-MT with dynamic retrieval in where the nearest-neighbour information is used and what it is meant to achieve?
What problem does the ROPO preference-optimization method address, and how is that different from the problem addressed by self-augmented preference optimization (SAPO)?
Name one way to improve a dense retriever using a cross-encoder teacher, and one way to adapt a dense retriever to a new domain when only a short text description of that domain is available.
Name two different ways to reduce overconfidence in language models: one that combines several viewpoints to estimate confidence, and one that passes reasoning from a larger model to a smaller one.

Which two LLM-based Text-to-SQL approaches improve results by retrieving demonstrations with the needed logical operators and by handling the wide tables of financial databases, and what does each report?
Name one cause of a knowledge-edited language model collapsing after a single ROME edit, and one way edited models still fail on reasoning questions. How was each addressed?
Does picking the languages carefully always work better than picking them at random?
What if a person edits the text afterwards?
Is there a way for it to check its own answer and look things up again?

note: Relevance labels are incomplete (pooling, PLAN.md section 7); recall and MRR are conservative. Unanswerable items are excluded. One run per condition. Timings are the wall-clock time of retriever.search on the machine that ran it, not a latency benchmark (PLAN.md section 4.4).
